problem_statement: A refactor binding arguments through ProcDef.params can collapse opaque formal names or lose default/rest/link roles. Exposing a full activation owner for source assistance would give topology an unrelated runtime authority.
question: Can a readonly procedure signature expose exact native formal bytes and binding ordinals while keeping activation entry private?
conclusion: SignatureSourceFormalParameters retains the original ParamList Key, exact ordered ByteFormalParameter values and the independently selected required/default/rest/link grammar. AnalysisResult issues it only for an exact retained declaration and unanimous Registry-selected declaration recipe. The facade preserves producer image/channel and full parser configuration; it neither installs formals nor proves command liveness, caller identity, cell contents, physical frame, native objects or Normal completion. Readonly worker parameter syntax may parse a genuine complete original operand with an independently selected dialect; the caller retains the separate ParamList role obligation. Name and optional second fields retain actual native list-child inputs and only independently mapped original source extents. Escape-produced parent values or mismatched clipped fields do not manufacture lexical child geometry. Readonly parameter-list values may retain actual lambda/list-child inputs without becoming complete lexical keys. Intermediate static list ancestry supplies source extents only when every traversed child preserves its literal bytes; evaluated or decoded intermediate values abstain. The complete-word and readonly-value facades share one field projection and the existing native formal parser.
scope: Rust readonly original formal metadata for explicit C Tcl and Jim source recipes. A fixed all-six model test covers opaque native names, default and rest binding counts and source/configuration mismatch. Native installation and formal storage observations remain separate.

tests.assertion: Keeps opaque bytes/default/rest topology and rejects changed source channel/image/full configuration.

An actual original lambda child retains its parent lineage, counted opaque name/default fields and mapped nested literal extents; a quoted decoded parent keeps readonly field bytes without inventing source spans or a complete child Word key.
